Good afternoon, dear colleagues. I'm sorry for being late. The 26th meeting, 26th and last meeting of the 2026 session of the Committee on Non-Governmental Organizations is called to order. Distinguished delegates, as you are aware, The Committee finished its substantive work on 29 May. You may also recall that at the same meeting, the Committee authorized Vice Chair Mr. Enes Tanriyevan to finalize the report in consultations with the members of the Committee, as appropriate. I now would like to invite Mr. Tanriyevan to introduce the report of the Committee Under Agenda Item 10, please.

I thank you, Chair. Distinguished delegates, I am pleased to present to you today the finalized report of the Committee on Non-Governmental Organizations on its 2026 resumed session. After 463 applications for consultative status before the Committee, the Committee recommended 90 for consultative status and deferred 322 applications for further consideration at its resumed session. Of the 547 new quadrennial reports, along with 167 deferred reports before the Committee, the Committee took note of 521 reports. 49 applications were closed without prejudice after the NGOs in question had failed to respond to queries by the deadline of 2 business days before the beginning of the Committee session. The draft report reflects discussions held during this session on a number of sensitive issues. I believe we have before us a balanced text that reflects faithfully the positions of members of the Committee. The report contains a number of draft decisions on matters calling for action by the Economic and Social Council. And I believe we have one small request to amend the draft report as of this afternoon, which is to remove the quotation marks from paragraph 21, which is in page 62. I assume that it will be okay with the committee members. It is— I assume it's technical edit. In that case, I wish to sincerely thank all delegations for their perseverance, patience, and goodwill, all of which were abundantly demonstrated during the informal consultations. It gives me pleasure to submit the draft report to the Committee for its consideration. I thank you.

I thank Mr. Tanri Joven. Distinguished delegates. Given the fact that all interested parties were consulted on the text of the report, may I propose that we adopt it as a whole. May I take it that the Committee is ready to adopt the report as orally revised? I hear no objection. It is so decided. Before proceeding to the closure of meeting, I know that the delegation of Israel would like to take the floor. The floor is yours.

Thank you, Chair. As this will be my final session of the Committee on governmental organizations, I would like to take a moment to express my sincere appreciation to all those who make the work of this Committee possible. Over the course of 9 sessions spanning a little more over than 4 years, I have had the privilege of working alongside dedicated members of the Secretariat, fellow Committee members, and many representatives of civil society organizations. Who have engaged with the process. I thank each of you and your professionalism, your commitment, and your contribution. The Committee on NGOs occupies a unique and important place within the UN system. It serves as a bridge between member states and civil society, helping to ensure that diverse voices can contribute to the work of the organization. This responsibility requires us to act with fairness, consistency and integrity. As I conclude my service on this committee, it is my hope that its work will continue to be guided by professionalism and objectivity, free from politicization that we have unfortunately witnessed at times, particularly over the past year. Civil society organizations should not operate under a sense of reprisal or fear that different that deferring views may lead to disproportionate consequences. When concerns arise regarding an organization, they should be addressed through the appropriate procedures and tools available to the Committee and to the UN system. We should remember that serious measures should be considered only after all available avenues have been exhausted and after due process has been respected. I also hope that the apparent bias that has too often affected Jewish and Israeli NGOs seeking to engage with the UN will finally be addressed. The United Nations should be a place where all legitimate civil society voices are heard. Jewish and Israeli organizations deserve the same opportunities as others to contribute their expertise, share their experiences, and participate meaningfully in UN forums. We must work to ensure that no organization is marginalized or effectively silenced because of its identity, nationality, or perspectives. For its part, Israel will continue to be a strong supporter of meaningful civil society participation throughout the UN system. We firmly believe that NGOs play a vital role in advancing the purpose and principles of the the UN, and in bringing expertise and innovation and voices of communities to our work. Israel will continue to support the participation of civil society in this committee, in drafting and implementation of resolutions, and across all UN forums where their contributions can strengthen our collective efforts. I leave this committee with gratitude for many colleagues and friends I have met along the way. And with hope that its future work will continue to uphold the principles upon which it was established. Thank you, Chair.

Thank you. Does any delegation wish to take the floor? I see none. Distinguished delegates, I declare this brings our meeting to an end, and I declare the 2026 session of the Committee on Non-Governmental Organizations Closed. The meeting is adjourned.
